name: sites
description: Publish a web page the agent built - a dashboard, a report, a landing page - at a real address on this instance, and decide who may open it: only you, the Project's people, any signed-in account, named guests, or everyone. The agent builds with its own toolchain and hands over the finished output; every publish is a separate release you can roll back to.

configSchema.label: Default visibility
configSchema.hint: What a newly created site is visible to before anyone changes it. A site never becomes public on its own; that is confirmed here in the app.

configSchema.label: Allow public sites
configSchema.hint: When off, every site requires signing in and the public option disappears from each site's access settings.

configSchema.label: Who may publish
configSchema.hint: Whether an ordinary account's agent may create and publish sites. Opening a site somebody shared is unaffected.

configSchema.label: Allow site runtimes
configSchema.hint: Let a site run Node, Bun, Python or TypeScript behind a private unix socket, or execute PHP through PHP-CGI. Every request runs in an isolated network namespace and requires isolated site hosting.
configSchema.help: A published runtime is code the agent wrote. It sees only its own release, runtime directory and the owner's sandbox HOME; it cannot reach the host loopback or another site's listener. It still runs under a user namespace rather than a separate VM and has no CPU or memory limit. Requests and responses are buffered, so streaming, server-sent events and websockets are not supported; request bodies are capped at 1 MB.

configSchema.label: Start timeout
configSchema.hint: How long a runtime has to answer after it is started before the publish is treated as failed.

configSchema.label: Request timeout
configSchema.hint: How long one exchange with a runtime may take in total before the visitor gets an error.

configSchema.label: Largest runtime response
configSchema.hint: A runtime answer is buffered whole before it is sent on, so this is a real ceiling.

configSchema.label: Largest file
configSchema.hint: Files larger than this are refused when publishing. A published file is held in memory while it is served, so this is a real ceiling rather than a preference.

configSchema.label: Largest site
configSchema.hint: Total size of one published release.

configSchema.label: Sites per account
configSchema.hint: How many sites one account may keep at once.

configSchema.label: Releases kept
configSchema.hint: Older releases beyond this count are removed. The release a site currently serves is never removed, whatever this is set to.

configSchema.label: Sign-in validity
configSchema.hint: How long a visitor stays signed in to a site before the browser is sent back through the sign-in step. Losing access takes effect immediately regardless of this, because permission is checked on every request.

configSchema.label: Contact email for certificates
configSchema.hint: A certificate authority requires a contact address to issue certificates and to warn about expiry. It is sent to the authority and stored nowhere else.
